title: Quantum Simulation on Riemannian Manifolds
authors: Dylan Herman, Jacob Watkins, Guneykan Ozgul, Jiayu Shen, Brandon Augustino, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Shouvanik Chakrabarti
abstract: We investigate algorithms for the quantum simulation of the Schrödinger equation on a Riemannian manifold, where the kinetic operator is defined by the Laplace--Beltrami operator corresponding to the metric. Our first algorithms are based on a global spectral method based on the identification of an efficient transform to the eigenbasis of the Laplace--Beltrami operator. We use this method to provide explicit, efficient, quantum simulation algorithms for the Riemannian Schrödinger equation on tori and spheres with their standard metrics, simplices with the Wright--Fisher metric, truncated positive orthants and their invertible affine images with the log-barrier Hessian metric, and $\ell_p$ balls with a metric induced by the Duffy map. Our second algorithm is based on a coherent simulation of local spectral methods on multiple charts, and is in principle applicable to any compact manifold. We first analyze this algorithm in the continuum and derive conditions under which a polynomial spectral cutoff suffices. We also provide a discretization analysis of a polynomial spectral cutoff for tensor-products of constant-dimensional manifolds. Finally, we consider applications of these methods to optimization and physical simulation. For optimization, we provide results including a generalization and convergence analysis of Quantum Hamiltonian Descent for geodesically convex functions that leads to explicit algorithms on the sphere and simplex, and a Riemannian generalization of the Real-Space Adiabatic Algorithm. For physical simulation, we show that our algorithms can simulate certain spatially discretized field theories, including a variant of the nonlinear sigma model.
summary: This paper develops quantum algorithms to simulate quantum dynamics governed by the Schrödinger equation on Riemannian manifolds. It introduces two primary techniques—a global spectral method and a local, chart-based coherent simulation—to handle the complex geometry. The work demonstrates the feasibility of these methods for simulating physical models ranging from constrained optimization problems to nonlinear field theories.
main_problem: Developing efficient quantum algorithms to simulate the time evolution governed by the Schrödinger equation on a Riemannian manifold.
main_result: The authors present two main algorithmic approaches: a global spectral method for specific manifolds and a coherent simulation of local spectral methods applicable to any compact manifold.
method: The methods involve spectral decomposition using the Laplace-Beltrami operator's eigenbasis (global method) or decomposing the manifold into overlapping local charts and coherently recombining local simulations (coherent-chart method).
model_or_system: The system is described by the Riemannian Schrödinger equation, $i\partial_t\psi = H_g\psi$, where the Hamiltonian includes the Laplace-Beltrami operator ($\Delta_g$) derived from the manifold metric $g$. Applications include optimization on curved spaces and simulating field theories like the nonlinear sigma model.
key_observables: The time evolution of the quantum state $\psi(t)$, and convergence/error guarantees related to the spectral cutoff used in the simulation.
important_parameters: The choice of manifold (e.g., sphere, torus, simplex), the metric tensor $g$, and the spectral cutoff parameter.
main_assumptions: The global method requires an efficient transform to the eigenbasis, while the coherent-chart method relies on deriving conditions for polynomial spectral cutoffs in the continuum limit.
paper_structure: The paper is structured around presenting and analyzing two distinct quantum simulation algorithms: the global spectral method and the coherent-chart method. It then applies these methods to specific physical problems, namely quantum optimization (e.g., Quantum Hamiltonian Descent) and physical field theory simulations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the computational challenge of simulating quantum dynamics on curved spaces, which is crucial for modeling physical systems whose configuration space is inherently Riemannian (e.g., particle motion on curved surfaces or field theories on curved backgrounds).
